C1.worst_defect: The hero subcopy is a four-line centred paragraph ('VendurePOS is an open-source till for Vendure, the open-source headless commerce framework. It is made for shops ... keeps selling when the connection drops.'). Under it come three CTAs plus a two-line note, so the eye has to get through about seven lines of grey text before reaching the screenshot.

C2.worst_defect: The comparison table's 'Live demo' cell says the demo sends 'anonymous usage events to ph.wcpos.com'. That is a domain from a different product, and the cell never says why. It is honest, but it reads as an unexplained third party inside a trust table.
C2.where: home.desktop.02, 'Live demo or your own store' table, last row

C3.worst_defect: Step 3 asks the reader to create two TypeScript files (src/generate-migration.ts and src/run-migrations.ts) and run them, and then puts the one-line 'npx vendure migrate' alternative for @vendure/create projects in a callout below them. A reader with the default scaffold goes through the long path before finding the short one.
C3.where: quick-start.desktop.01-02, '3. Generate and run the migration' and the 'Other ways to run the migration' callout

C4.worst_defect: The Troubleshooting right rail nests three levels deep (At the counter > Act on a header notice > Orders line / Till updates line / When till updates need attention / Store settings) across 17 entries. Most of the page's headings are quoted error strings, so it scans as a wall of quotation marks, not as a list of symptoms.
C4.where: troubleshooting.desktop.01, 'On this page' rail and 'Act on a header notice'

C5.worst_defect: The three till screenshots on At the till use three different widths. The payment screen fills the 836 px column, the cashier sheet is a ~380 px card centred with about 70 px of extra empty space above it and its caption hanging left under the centred image, and the closure is a ~510 px centred card. The page's figure rhythm looks accidental.
C5.where: at-the-till.desktop.02 (payment, full width) vs at-the-till.desktop.03 (cashier sheet, y≈830-1240) vs at-the-till.desktop.04 (closure, y≈330-870)

C6.worst_defect: The phone hero screenshot is the till's phone layout cropped to two product cards. The category chip row is clipped at the right edge ('Gif'), and the cart and €20.09 total named in the alt text are never visible, so a phone visitor sees a search box and two tiles, not a sale.

C7.worst_defect: The share card crops the till screenshot through the middle of the first product row: the 'In Stock' pills under Canvas Apron to Cotton Beanie are sliced at the bottom edge, and the cart pane ends on a half-visible 'Order discount' button.

overall_worst.defect: On At the till, the only docs page with screenshots, the three figures are set at three unrelated widths (full column, ~380 px centred, ~510 px centred). The narrow ones also carry extra empty space above them and left-hung captions, so the cashier guide's visual rhythm breaks at every figure.
overall_worst.fix: Put every till screenshot in the same figure frame: full content width with the card centred on a neutral backdrop, or one fixed max-width. Use the same top and bottom margins for all of them and centre each caption under its image.
